title: Session-consent scrubbing + query-level RBAC and tiered retention for observability
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Motivation:
Several customers (enterprise and regulated) have requested fine-grained controls over what observability data is retained and who can query it. The current platform-level retention and coarse redaction rules are insufficient for: (1) per-session consent (users can request scrubbing for a session or dataset), (2) query-level RBAC so support engineers can only run scoped queries, and (3) tiered retention where sensitive fields are stored only in short-term hot storage and aggregated for long-term analytics.

Goal:
Implement a platform capability that enables: (A) session-consent based scrubbing and reversible, auditable unredaction for authorized support flows; (B) query-level RBAC enforced at the observability query gateway (metrics/traces/logs); (C) configurable tiered retention policies by tenant and sensitivity label; (D) full audit trail and access logging for any access/unredaction event.

Non-goals:
- Replacing existing telemetry ingestion pipeline (we will extend it).
- Implementing full consent UI in the Console (we will provide APIs and a basic Console toggle for admins).

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Redaction model: prefer deterministic field-level masking with reversible encryption for a short TTL (KMS-backed envelope keys) rather than full irreversible hashing to allow just-in-time support unredaction. This increases risk profile; require JIT access approval (see security controls) and short-lived audit tokens.
- Query-level RBAC: enforce at the query gateway with policy evaluation (OPA-style) using token scopes and query AST reputation checks to prevent data exfiltration via crafted queries (e.g., sampling + group-by attacks). Adds CPU to gateway, but keeps downstream stores simpler.
- Retention tiers: hot (7d full fidelity), warm (30d partially redacted), cold (90d aggregated/rollup). Tenants can configure policies; defaults will map to compliance tiers (e.g., HIPAA customers pick shorter hot window).
- Cost vs fidelity: more aggressive redaction reduces storage and access risk but harms debugging. We'll provide sampling knobs and a "debug mode" that preserves full fidelity when enabled for a limited time-window and audited.

Operational constraints:
- Must not increase tail latency for 95th/99th trace queries beyond SLA by >5%.
- All unredaction events must create immutable audit events that are replicated to a separate audit log cluster with stricter retention and encryption.

Acceptance_criteria:
acceptance_criteria: Admin can configure per-tenant retention tiers and sensitivity labels from Console or API
On ingestion, telemetry records are labeled and routed to appropriate retention tier and redaction stage
Support engineers can request JIT unredaction which triggers an approval workflow and audit entry; unredaction artifacts are short-lived (TTL configurable) and logged
Query Gateway rejects any query that violates tenant RBAC policy and returns 403 with clear reason code
Audit log contains immutable record for each access, including actor, justification, time, and query fingerprint
End-to-end tests validate that hot/warm/cold policies enforce expected visibility and that aggregated rollups match full data within acceptable error bounds
tasks: Spike: prototype reversible field encryption with KMS envelopes and TTL rotation (ENG spike) - 3d
Implement query-gateway policy hooks and AST-level inspection (engine work) - 5d
Add sensitivity labeling step to ingestion pipeline and routing to retention tiers - 4d
Console: admin pages for retention policy, JIT unredaction requests, and audit UI (basic) - 5d
Security: define approval flow and integrate with SSO/Access Approvals; schedule security review - 2d
E2E integration tests and performance tests (latency/regression) - 3d
Migration job: backfill recent 30d data into warm tier with labels for 5 pilot tenants - 2d
Run internal pilot with two enterprise customers; collect feedback and iterate - 7d
